samples.summary: Reset-color test cannot distinguish `{color: undefined}` from `{}` — the exact distinction the fix depends on
samples.evidence: `expect(editor.applyStyle).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ color: undefined })` (and the backgroundColor twin at line 87) uses vitest's `equals`, which — like `toEqual` — ignores properties whose value is `undefined`. A regression that dropped the key entirely (`applyStyle({})`) would still satisfy this assertion. That matters because the store's `removedInlineStyleAttrs` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:147) removes an attribute only when `key in style && style[key] === undefined`; an omitted key is a silent no-op reset. The test only really rules out the old `""` value. Asserting on `applyStyle.mock.calls[0][0]` with `'color' in arg` would close the gap.

samples.summary: The new non-finite guard in `parseBlockStyle` (the legacy-document read path) has no test
samples.evidence: `parseBlockStyle` was changed to skip attributes whose `Number(...)` is not finite, and `alignment` is now only taken when `typeof attrs.alignment === 'string'`. The comment explicitly motivates this with "a document written before the serializer above" (i.e. existing CRDTs holding the literal string "undefined"). The only new test (docs-tree.spec.ts:98 'falls back to the block defaults for a partial style') exercises the WRITE path via `writeDocsRoot` with `style: {}`, which now never emits those attributes — so the read-side guard is never hit. Nothing constructs a tree whose block attrs contain `lineHeight: "undefined"`/`"abc"` and asserts the defaults come back instead of NaN.

samples.summary: The PPTX `ALGN` and `UNDERLINE_STYLE_TO_U` object→Map hardening ships untested
samples.evidence: Both lookups were converted to `Map` specifically so a persisted `toString`/`constructor` alignment or underlineStyle cannot resolve through the prototype chain into `<a:pPr algn>` / `u="…"`. The DOCX counterpart got a dedicated `it.each(['toString','constructor','valueOf','__proto__','hasOwnProperty'])` suite (packages/docs/test/export/docx-style-map.test.ts), but grepping packages/slides/test/export/pptx/text.test.ts for `toString`/`constructor`/`__proto__`/`underlineStyle` finds only the pre-existing 'dashed' round-trip at line 61. The slides hardening therefore has no regression guard at all.

samples.summary: `applyCellSpan`'s switch to node-scoped removal has no nested-table test, though that is the stated regression
samples.evidence: The diff replaced the path-range `removeStyleByPath(cellPath, endPath, …)` in `applyCellSpan` with `removeCellNodeStyle`, justified by "a path range would drop `colSpan`/`rowSpan` from every nested-table cell inside this one too". The new tests only cover the analogous case for `applyCellStyle`/`backgroundColor` (yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:2033, 2053); the `applyCellSpan` describe block (line 2069 onward) still only exercises single-level tables, so nothing would fail if the range form were restored there. A test nesting a table inside the cell, giving the inner cell a colSpan, then clearing the outer cell's span, is missing.
searchedFor: grep nested in the same file

samples.summary: The docs toolbar and table context-menu reset call sites changed to `undefined` with no test
samples.evidence: `docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx` (`handleTextColor(undefined)` / `handleHighlightColor(undefined)`) and `docs-table-context-menu.tsx` (`applyTableCellStyle({ backgroundColor: undefined })`) were changed away from `""`, but the only new UI test (packages/frontend/tests/components/text-formatting/color-reset.test.ts) renders `TextFormatGroup` — a different component. Nothing exercises the docs toolbar's or the table menu's reset handlers, so a revert to `""` there would go unnoticed.

samples.summary: Two of the three assertions in the new partial-style test are tautological or unfalsifiable
samples.evidence: `expect(typeof value === 'number' ? Number.isFinite(value) : true).toBe(true)` degenerates to `expect(true).toBe(true)` for every non-numeric field. `expect(JSON.stringify(style)).not.toContain('undefined')` cannot fail for the failure mode described in the comment either: `JSON.stringify` omits `undefined`-valued keys and serializes `NaN` as `null`, so only a literal `"undefined"` string value would trip it — and that is already excluded by `expect(style.alignment).toBe('left')`. Asserting `style` equals `DEFAULT_BLOCK_STYLE` would be a real check.

samples.summary: 'accepts a partial block style' asserts only that an injected mock rejection propagates
samples.evidence: The test mocks `documentService.getDocumentOrThrow` to reject with a sentinel `NotFoundException` and asserts that exception comes back. It does distinguish validation failure (BadRequestException) from success, but it asserts nothing about the partial style being accepted/normalized downstream, and the controller change in this diff is comment-only — so the test guards no new behavior.

`styleColor` now routes through `toRgbHexColor`, which returns `undefined` for `rgba(…, 0)` / `#RRGGBB00`, making those export as black. The added tests cover `rgb()`, `#RGB` and the wrapped srgb form but not the transparency branch, which is the one behavior change most likely to surprise (an invisible run painting black in the PDF).

finding.summary: Reset-color test cannot distinguish `{color: undefined}` from `{}` — the exact distinction the fix depends on
finding.evidence: `expect(editor.applyStyle).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ color: undefined })` (and the backgroundColor twin at line 87) uses vitest's `equals`, which — like `toEqual` — ignores properties whose value is `undefined`. A regression that dropped the key entirely (`applyStyle({})`) would still satisfy this assertion. That matters because the store's `removedInlineStyleAttrs` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:147) removes an attribute only when `key in style && style[key] === undefined`; an omitted key is a silent no-op reset. The test only really rules out the old `""` value. Asserting on `applyStyle.mock.calls[0][0]` with `'color' in arg` would close the gap.

verdict.reason: The quoted assertions do exist and vitest's non-strict equals would indeed also accept applyStyle({}), but the test is not vacuous and the residual gap is not blocking under this lens. The regression guarded is the pre-fix applyStyle({ color: "" }) (root cause documented at docs/tasks/active/20260812-docs-font-color-reset-todo.md:11-14); { color: "" } is NOT equal to { color: undefined } under equals, so reverting text-format-group.tsx:130/252 and 315/347 makes the test fail. The test renders the real TextFormatGroup + ColorPickerGrid with only the editor as the mocked boundary, so no over-mocking. Separately, the "key present and undefined => removeStyleByPath" semantics of removedInlineStyleAttrs (yorkie-doc-store.ts:144-163) is genuinely exercised at the store layer by yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:628-668, which applies color/backgroundColor/fontFamily/bold as explicit undefined and asserts the attributes actually leave the Tree while a non-cleared key survives; the plan doc (lines 24-26) states that store behavior is pre-existing. The remaining gap is a hypothetical different regression (rewriting the object literal to omit the key), i.e. "the assertion could be stricter" — minor hardening, not a behavior change shipped with fake coverage nor a behavior change with no meaningful test.

finding.summary: The new non-finite guard in `parseBlockStyle` (the legacy-document read path) has no test
finding.evidence: `parseBlockStyle` was changed to skip attributes whose `Number(...)` is not finite, and `alignment` is now only taken when `typeof attrs.alignment === 'string'`. The comment explicitly motivates this with "a document written before the serializer above" (i.e. existing CRDTs holding the literal string "undefined"). The only new test (docs-tree.spec.ts:98 'falls back to the block defaults for a partial style') exercises the WRITE path via `writeDocsRoot` with `style: {}`, which now never emits those attributes — so the read-side guard is never hit. Nothing constructs a tree whose block attrs contain `lineHeight: "undefined"`/`"abc"` and asserts the defaults come back instead of NaN.

verdict.reason: The non-finite guard in parseBlockStyle (docs-tree.ts:183-187) and the `typeof attrs.alignment === 'string'` gate (line 177) exist as described. parseBlockStyle is not exported, so it is only reachable via readDocsRoot; a repo-wide grep for readDocsRoot yields exactly three test files (docs-tree.spec.ts, docs-tree-attached.e2e-spec.ts, docs-font-styles-attached.e2e-spec.ts), and all three construct their trees solely through writeDocsRoot from valid DocsDocument objects. Because serializeBlockStyle (lines 162-168) already drops non-string alignment and non-finite numbers on write, no test ever puts a "undefined"/"abc" attribute into the tree, so the read-side guard's Number.isFinite branch is never taken. The cited test (docs-tree.spec.ts:98-124) exercises only the write path with `style: {}`, where `field in attrs` is false; its loop assertion is additionally vacuous for non-numeric values. No hand-built ElementNode/Tree with raw block attrs exists anywhere in packages/backend/test or src (greps for attributes/new Tree(/editBulkByPath/NaN/isFinite came up empty). The frontend's separate parseBlockStyle (yorkie-doc-store.ts:217) is a different module and cannot cover the backend function. This is a behavior change on the legacy-document read path shipped with no test that can fail if the guard is removed — major under the missing-tests limb of the test-adequacy rubric.
